title: Why the world's first spinal cord transplant is so controversial | New Scientist
description: A spinal cord transplant happened in people for the first time during a surgery in Russia, but the evidence underpinning it is lacking
author: New Scientist

title: There may be a new dwarf planet just beyond Pluto | New Scientist
description: Astronomers spotted what appears to be a dwarf planet in the outer solar system using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory – if confirmed, it joins a small and exclusive club
author: Leah Crane

title: Access to stone as well as water governed where early humans lived | New Scientist
description: The sands of the Arabian peninsula were once dotted with lakes that teemed with life, but early humans avoided them unless they came with easy access to stone for tool-making
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Transplanted ovaries adjust to the recipient's biological age | New Scientist
description: Ovaries from older mice, which were no longer able to reproduce, seemed to become active again when transplanted into younger animals, suggesting the new host's body lowered the organs' molecular age
author: James Woodford

title: Super-insulating solid may soon help old homes reach net-zero goals | New Scientist
description: Millions of old homes across the UK and Europe need insulating under net-zero strategies, and promising start-ups believe materials called aerogels could be the answer
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science | New Scientist
description: A central tenet in computer science has apparently been disproven by OpenAI, a result that will force textbooks to be rewritten if it is confirmed
author: Chris Stokel-Walker
